title.narrative: CO- Drought Response in Awdal & Bari

description.narrative:
Oxfam, in partnership with community structures, proposes to reach 10,104 individuals (3,234 women, 2,627 men, 2,223 girls, and 2,020 boys) affected by the current drought crisis in Lughaya district in Awdal region of Somaliland and Iskushuban district in Bari region of Puntland. The intervention responds to a spike in humanitarian need as the conditions and effects of drought worsen, in the context of a protracted climate-induced crisis, compounded by conflict-related displacement in Puntland. The project targets a mixedpopulation of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host communities, with IDPs representing the majority (6,708 people), as well as a focus on households with people with disabilities (1,225 individuals). The response will be delivered across two sectors: Protection and Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), using an integrated approach. Vulnerable households in Lughaya district in Awdal, Somaliland and Iskushuban district in Bari, Puntland will receive multipurpose cash transfers to cover essential needs while also benefiting from protection-focused interventions including urgent cash support for high-risk cases, dissemination of lifesaving protection messages, activation of community protection volunteers, strengthened referral pathways, and distribution of solar lights to improve safety and dignity. The most important impact of the project will be that drought-affected households are able to meet urgent basic needs through cash assistance while at the same time strengthening community-based protection mechanisms and reducingprotection risks, particularly for women, children, and people with disabilities. The project will reach a total of 10,104 individuals in Lughaya district in Awdal region of Somaliland and Iskushuban district in Bari region of Puntland. Of these, 7,200 people will benefit from protection support and 2,904 people from multipurpose cash assistance. Women and girls make up nearly half of all beneficiaries, while 6,708 are internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 1,225 are people with disabilities, ensuring strong focus on themost vulnerable groups
Overall Project Objective:
To strengthen the ability of 10,104 drought-affected individuals in Somaliland and Puntland to meet their essential needs, access timely protection, and live with greater safety and dignity – especially among women, children, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and persons with disabilities – through accessing multipurpose cash and targetedprotection services The proposed intervention is fully aligned with the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan, specifically addressing priority gaps in food security, protection, and cash assistance in re-prioritized districts of Somaliland and Puntland. Oxfam activelyparticipate in national and state-level coordination structures, including the Area Based Coordination at district level, Food Security, Protection, and WASH Clusters, and the Cash Working Group, contributing to joint needs assessments, collective cash delivery models, and advocacy efforts. A robust MEAL system will be tailored, ensuring it is aligned to the project objective. The system willbe informed and guided by Oxfam’s CAMSA which provides a structured approach to effective project monitoring and social accountability. The project LF has been carefully designed to enable systematic tracking of project performance and immediate impacts on the lives of the drought affected communities in the targeted districts of Lughaya and Iskushuban. A comprehensive MEAL plan will be developed at project outset to further define the indicators, data collection approaches, tools and responsibilities for tracking progress against key results indicators. The project output level achievements will be tracked on monthly basis using the output tracker system. The number of people reached and achievement against key project results etc. will be compiled and shared in a monthly Sitrep.Data collection and analysis will be done separately for women, men, children, PLWDs and by age. Field level MEAL officers will conduct regular monitoring visits in coordination with sector leads. Oxfam is committed to ensuring accountability to affected populations in all stages of the project cycle. This includes timely and transparent sharing of project information with communities and other relevant stakeholders to foster trust, participation and ownership. We will establish a context-specific and appropriate community feedback mechanism (CFM) to enable affected women, girls, boys and men to express feedback,express their concerns and influence decision-making.
Overall, This project seeks to address these immediate, life-saving gaps by reaching 10,104 drought affected individuals with protection and multipurpose cash assistance in two of the hardest-hit districts of Somaliland (Lughaya, Awdal) and Puntland (Iskushuban, Bari) dignity – especially among women, children, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and persons with disabilities – through accessing multipurpose cash and targeted protection services.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
